chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Qutaybah al-A'sha, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sacrifices of the Jews and the Christians, so he said: 'The sacrifice (dhabīḥah) is a name, and one cannot be trusted regarding the name except the Muslim.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the meat of Jews and Christians based on the meaning of 'sacrifice'?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the theological distinction between the general linguistic term 'dhabīḥah' and the specific religious validity of the sacrifice. He asserts that while the act of slaughter may be physically similar, the trustworthiness (*amanah*) of the sacrificer is contingent upon their faith, implying that non-Muslims cannot be trusted to uphold the religious sanctity of the act. This reflects the Shia juristic view that the validity of *dhabīḥah* often hinges on the sacrificer's adherence to Islamic creed, distinguishing it from the permissibility of eating the food of the People of the Book.
